To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) sex differences in play preferences are already present at age 3 and are quite stable; (b) these sex differences are related to the development of sex role stereotyped behavior; and (c), the development of visual-spatial ability is related to involvement with masculine activities in boys.

(a) sex-typing of activity preference is already well established in nursery-school-age children; (b) the development of sex-typing appears to be related to the avoidance of opposite sex activities; and ( c) the development of masculine activity preference appears to be related, at least in part, to the development of spatial ability in boys.
Masculine and feminine activities in the nursery school classroom are related to other classroom behaviors and cognitive abilities.
